deepseek_columns.ai_commands: curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/SessionService/Sessions 2>&1 | jq ".Members[]?.Id, .Members[]?.UserName, .Members[]?.Oem" 2>/dev/null; echo ---ipmi---; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" session info 2>&1 | head
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return FULL Redfish SessionService session list + IPMI session info so the user confirms each active session/IP is shown correctly; forcibly disconnecting a session is a write the user drives.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: reading sessions is read-only; disconnecting a session (write) is user-driven and could log out management access.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL correctly separates listing from disconnect risk, but its collection is not full: Redfish collection members commonly require per-member retrieval and pagination, `head` truncates IPMI evidence, `session info` may describe only one IPMI session, TLS/credentials are insecure and neither command validates the displayed client IP nor performs the required isolated disconnect.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly requires complete paginated inventory, redaction, cross-protocol correlation, protected/current-session identification, an independent recovery path and one explicitly approved test-session disconnect. V3.1 additionally requires a controlled known-client source-IP fixture so `IP show correct` has an authoritative expected value.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 920/2291 accepts the truncated command conditionally but does not define session namespace, IP source/NAT normalization, pagination/member expansion, token handling, disconnect target, remaining-session health or audit proof.
historical_reviews.related_source_cases: Concurrent KVM, WebUI login/logout and account-management rows have different resources and cannot prove active SessionService inventory or termination. Redfish and IPMI session IDs are not inherently cross-addressable.

historical_reviews.v3: No V3 overlay exists for this exact case.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves the concise IP/display/disconnect source; ED-34 treats protocol, fields and expected IP as Project inputs; ED-35 keeps actual disconnect coverage instead of read-only listing; ED-38 requires approval, independent access, one target and no automatic retry.

original_test_intent: Verify the BMC session-management view accurately lists an intentionally created management session with the expected client/source IP and identity metadata, and can disconnect exactly that approved non-critical session without terminating protected or recovery access.
original_method: Create or identify a controlled test session from a known client/source address, retrieve the complete BMC WebUI/Redfish session collection and supported IPMI session information, expand/paginate and normalize identifiers/user/client IP/protocol/timing, compare the target against the independent client/network fixture, then disconnect that single session through the supported control after approval and confirm termination plus unaffected remaining access and audit evidence.
manual_activity: An engineer defines the session types/fields and expected client-IP fixture, identifies protected sessions and approves one test-session disconnect. A human may create/observe the source WebUI session and retain independent recovery. Automation can collect/correlate inventory and verify termination, but cannot choose a session to kill or issue the verdict.
required_inputs: BMC/firmware/WebUI/Redfish/IPMI identity and supported session-resource semantics
Known test client, account/role, source address and network/NAT/proxy path that defines the expected displayed IP
In-scope session types and complete fields/pagination/member retrieval requirements
Controlled non-critical session ID/token correlation with secret-redaction policy
Explicit list of current/admin/recovery/system sessions that must not be terminated
Supported single-session disconnect action, audit event and expected client-side behavior
Independent recovery/admin access and post-disconnect inventory/health evidence
safety_requirements: Do not clear BMC/audit logs or expose passwords, tokens, cookies, full usernames or unnecessary client IP data in artifacts.
Use validated TLS and secret handling; do not use `curl -k`, command-line passwords or truncated output as formal evidence.
Expand every collection member and pagination link before claiming a complete inventory; do not assume Redfish and IPMI sessions share identifiers or fields.
Verify the target session against a known client/user/IP and identify current/recovery/protected sessions before presenting a disconnect.
Obtain point-of-action approval for one non-critical session only; never bulk-delete or terminate a system/service/current recovery session.
Verify disconnect from the target client and an independent administrator, preserve the audit event and stop without retry on wrong-session loss or broader access impact.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target/schema, controlled client/IP fixture, session namespaces/fields, protected sessions, disconnect action, independent recovery and redaction.
Collect complete member-expanded paginated WebUI/Redfish and supported IPMI inventories, normalize metadata and explain expected cross-protocol differences.
After explicit confirmation, disconnect one designated test session and verify its client loses access while independent admin and protected sessions remain healthy.
Archive redacted before/after/audit evidence and stop without insecure TLS, truncation, bulk termination, automatic retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Define expected client IP/address normalization and in-scope session types/fields for this firmware.
Identify protected/current/recovery sessions and approve exactly one controlled test-session disconnect plus recovery.
Review full inventory, IP correlation, disconnect and unaffected-access evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The list/read idea is relevant but the actual commands are incomplete and insecure: collection members may not contain expanded fields, pagination is ignored, IP fields are not selected, IPMI output is truncated, and no disconnect is exercised. It cannot meet either source checkpoint.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the target firmware's discovered SessionService members with pagination and protected TLS, plus the supported UI/IPMI inventory. Disconnect only the explicitly approved member/session through the vendor-supported single-session action.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Sessions identity, correct-IP and disconnect wording, no Script, DeepSeek curl/jq/ipmitool proposal/risk and 2/0-minute estimates remain preserved; Review does not promote those estimates to a disconnect timeout.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create a known-source test session, prove complete BMC inventory and correct normalized client IP, then terminate exactly that session under approval and verify independent access/audit state.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected BMC firmware's WebUI/Redfish/IPMI session implementation and known management-network path.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC/WebUI/Redfish schema, IPMI client/library, browser/client and proxy/NAT versions/configuration.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor SessionService/session-management specification, Project privacy/redaction and privileged-access policy, network address model and recovery SOP.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes `IP correct` measurable with a fixture and adds complete collection semantics, isolated disconnect, privacy and recovery while retaining both source checkpoints.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A Redfish collection may omit IPMI/KVM/SOL sessions; IPMI info may not cover WebUI sessions; list disappearance alone does not prove client invalidation; read-only inventory does not satisfy disconnect.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Schema, expected client IP/path, test/protected sessions, disconnect action, redaction and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Wrong-target termination can remove management access; proxy/NAT can legitimately change displayed IP; session metadata is security-sensitive.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use WebUI, Redfish or a vendor tool for inventory/disconnect when the original visible-IP and disconnect checkpoints, actual namespace, reason, approval and uncovered interfaces are recorded. A read-only override is partial evidence and cannot claim disconnect passed.
expected_evidence: Target/version/schema capability, known test client/user/source/network path, expected normalized IP and protected-session/recovery inventory
Complete member-expanded paginated redacted session inventories with session ID, user/role, client IP, protocol, state and timing where supported
Cross-namespace mapping and explanation of legitimate Redfish/IPMI/WebUI differences plus proof the displayed test-client IP matches the fixture
Approved single-session disconnect request/audit and target-client rejection/closure with independent post-inventory showing protected sessions intact
No secret exposure/bulk action/retry, recovery disposition, coverage limits and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Title, Procedure and Criteria consistently require session IP display accuracy plus disconnect. Wording is sparse but contains no competing target or operation; expected IP, session namespace and disconnect semantics are Project/vendor readiness inputs.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The two session-management checkpoints are identifiable. A controlled client and vendor schema can define the expected IP and safe disconnect, so missing inputs do not make the review permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keeps PACKAGE but replaces incomplete insecure/truncated collection with a known-client full inventory and actual isolated disconnect proof.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on hybrid classification and strengthens authoritative expected-IP fixture, per-member retrieval and two-sided client/admin termination evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces command-exists sanity with complete namespace-aware inventory and a protected single-session state transition.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Keeps account management and other console/session-capacity cases outside this session-IP/disconnect verdict.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No invalid draft exists for this exact source identity.

review_improvement: Prevents truncated member references and a risky unspecified logout from being reported as correct session IP/display and disconnect behavior, while preserving a safe, independently observable functional termination checkpoint.
independent_technical_reasoning: Session inventories are protocol-specific and commonly expose sensitive member links rather than expanded records. A displayed IP is only testable against a known client and its NAT/proxy path. Disconnect success requires both target-client invalidation and continued independent administration; list disappearance alone can be timeout or filtering. Therefore the case needs a controlled fixture, complete enumeration and one isolated approved write.
